head:
Executive Orbet.
B)y reason of the small compensation usually paid to messenger boys
upon entrance to the service, and by reason of the early age at which they
are appointed, it has not been deemed proper to hold this examination for
the departmental service at Washington away from the seat of government.
The examination has been limited to Washington, D. C., but applicants,
while actually located in the District of Columlia, have been able to estab-
lish legal residence in the various States in so many instances that the
several States and Territories have been fairly represented in the appor-
tionment of messenger boys. Legal residents of the District of Columbia
have not been certified for the apportioned service. Under Section 7 of
the Census Act approved July 2, 190, it will be necessary for applicants to
actually reside in the State or Territory in which they are examined, and
as it is deemed impracticable to hold messenger boy examinations outside
of \'Va,ington, the examination will be limited by the Census Act to resi-
dents of the District of Columbia. If messenger boys were charged to
the apportionment as heretofore, the excessive number of apportioned
appointments already received by the District would be largely increased.
In viewv of these facts, Civil Service Rule VII, and Civil Service Rule XI
are hereby amended to provide for the appointment of messenger boys
without charge to the apportionment.
Civil Service Rule VII, paragraph 2, is amended by adding the fo

head:

Mr. Fred V. Murphy may be reinstated as an architectural draftsman
in the Office of the Supervising Architect of the Treasury, the time limit
for reinstatement being hereby waived.
Mr. Murphy wvas employed continuously in the Supervising Archi-
tect's Office from October 18, 1899, to June 30, 1905. He has, since
studied abroad, in the Ecole des Beaux Arts, Paris, at which institution he
has completed the course in architecture. The Secretary 'of the Treasury
believed that Mr. Murphy's six, years' experience in the Supervising Archi-
tect's Office and his four years' subsequent study and travel in Europe,
would render his services of unusual value. The Civil Service Commis-
sion recognized the validity of these reasons and joined the Secretary of
the Treasury in his recommendation, and stated as an additional reason for
the action proposed the depleted condition of the register for architectural
draftsman, which contained an insufficient number of eligibles for a full
certification.

machine_read.last_words: by the Civil Service Commission WM TAFT THE WHITE HOUSE March No

head:
Executive Orber.
James A. Compton, William E. Dulin, and George P. Meyer may be
reinstated in the Pension Office without regard to the fact that they have
been separated from the service for more than one year. This action is
based upon the statement of the Secretary of the Interior that under similar
circumstances separations from the service would not in general be imposed
for a similar offense and that the men suffered an injustice in their removal.
Their reinstatement is favored by the Civil Service Commission.
WM H TAFT
THE WHITE HOUSE,
March 15, 1910.
[No. 1177.]

head:
Executive Orber4
Schedule A, Subdivision VII, of the civil service rules, relating to
the Department of the Interior, is hereby amended by the addition of the
following paragraph:
23. One histopathologist temporarily engaged in research work
at the Government Hospital for the Insane.
This order is approved on the concurrent recommendation of the
Superintendent of the Government Hospital for the Insane and the Civil
Service Commission, in view of the fact that it would be difficult or impos-
sible to obtain persons with the required qualifications through competitive
examination and to enable the Government Hospital for the Insane to
avail itself of the services of advanced students of foreign laboratories for
nominal pay.
WM H TAFT
THE WHITE HOUSE,
Afarcit 23, 1910.
[No. ''79.]
